2. Its goldens in `harness/goldens/<ns>/` — success **and every error scenario**. **Open

against success-only goldens has an unverified error surface, and the UI branches on error metadata.


It replays the route on **every** scenario with the deterministic clock, seed and secret already set,
reads `harness/replay-report.json`, and prints GREEN or RED with the failing pointers.

## Step 4 — Flip

There is no separate flip step. `--flip` is applied by `verify` itself, and only when the report it
just read has zero failures and zero missing goldens over at least one comparison. An unreachable
target exits 3 and flips nothing — an API that is down is not a green route, and it is not a red one
either.

**Do not call `contracts/tools/set-implementation.mjs` by hand.** A flipped route is covered by the
local `--only-implemented` gate forever after; flipping a red route breaks the build for everyone,
and the whole point of routing the flip through the report is that no one has to be trusted to have
run the replay first.

Then the whole namespace:

```
node harness/port.mjs verify --namespace <ns>
```

sub-step multiplies the most expensive check in the program by the number of slices and tells you
nothing the module-level pass will not.
